Subject: Investor deck readiness: metrics sanity check & commit hygiene

Team —

We have the investor readout next Thursday and I want to lock the headline metrics by EOD tomorrow. Please do a quick sanity pass and update the shared Q2 metrics sheet I attached with the most defensible numbers (arr, bookings commit, recognized ARR bridge/backlog). Key asks:

- Sales: move any deals that are actually committed into HubSpot Commit stage and confirm PO/DocuSign envelope id. If legal sign-off or procurement is blocking, flag in column G.
- Finance: provide cohort ARR and churn reconciliation to support the headline ARR. Include any one-offs (credits/true-ups) as separate line items.
- Product/RevOps: confirm that Dedicated reserved contracts are modeled as ARR vs billings per contract terms.

Attachments: Q2_metrics_table.xlsx (template) — use tabs for ARR, bookings, churn.

My timeline: final numbers by 11:00 PT on Fri 19th. If you foresee any gaps or risk items for the narrative, call them out inline in the sheet and reply-all with the short rationale.

Thanks —
Markus

Subject: RE: Investor deck readiness: metrics sanity check & commit hygiene

Markus —

I've filled the template with the current reconciled numbers and flagged two items that need sales confirmation (row 14/23). Quick highlights:

- ARR (net, as of 6/30 projected): $32,400,000 (includes estimated ramp from pilot expansions we expect to recognize in Q3)
- Bookings commit (next 90 days with signed PO or binding agreement): $2,100,000
- Quarterly churn (cohort methodology): 0.8% — see tab "cohort_recon" for month-by-month churn schedule and cohorts by ARR bucket

Open questions I noted in the sheet: how we should treat the 24-month prepay with deferred revenue on the ARR headline (I left as recognized ARR per ASC guidance but marked as "prepay_note"). Also flagged a $125k credit that will hit this quarter (customer dispute) — shown as separate line.

Attachment: Q2_metrics_table_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)

On the Commit definition: should Sales move deals at LOI + legal explicitly to "Commit" or only after countersigned PO? I'm inclining to prefer countersigned PO for investor-facing numbers.

- Laura

Thanks Laura, Markus —

I've uploaded the sales commit list and reconciled against HubSpot. Summary: three net-new deals moved to "Commit" in the past 48h (HS-98122, HS-98190, HS-98234). HS-98234 has signed commercial terms but legal is still finishing a data residency addendum (procurement@acme.com is engaged). We expect countersign by Mon 22nd but I have it marked as "pending legal" in MAP_Commit_List.csv.

Notes:
- Pipeline hygiene: moved 18 stalled trials to "disqualified" per the 90-day inactivity rule — this tightened the commit conversion assumption by ~300k (best-case).
- ARR math: for multi-year deals, I'm using first 12 months to compute ARR; we should call out multi-year uplift separately in the slide notes.

Nice work. A few quick asks before finalizing the slide copy:

1) For investor-facing ARR headline, let's use recognized ARR (Laura's number) but include an early-visibility "contract backlog" callout with the bookings commit figure and expected recognition schedule.
2) Reduce our "best-case" uplift by 300k following Marissa's pipeline clean-up. Please reflect that in the narrative and the sensitivity table.
3) Marcus — can you provide a short bullet (1-2 lines) on any FX / discounts that materially move Q2 recognized ARR?

I'll draft the two narrative bullets for the deck (why ARR grew, and why next quarter looks strong) and attach version 2 of the narrative doc. Finals by Fri 11:00 PT please.

Attachment: Investor_Narrative_v2.docx

Thanks,
Karthik
